name: Yarumá
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.note: Extinct; only wordlists/ethnography (Krause, Levi-Strauss, de Carvalho comparative); no phonological description

sources.citation: Meira, Sérgio. 2006. Cariban languages. In K. Brown (ed.), Encyclopedia of Language and Linguistics, 2nd ed., vol. 2: 199-203. Oxford: Elsevier. (text../apal1257/)
sources.note: Family-level remarks on rhythmic vs. penultimate stress in living Cariban languages; Yarumá not mentioned (grep).

sources.citation: Loukotka, Čestmír. 1968. Classification of South American Indian Languages. Los Angeles: UCLA Latin American Center. (archive.org scanned../tive1236/)
sources.note: Nothing; 'Yaruma or Aruma... now perhaps extinct. [Meyer in Krause 1936, pp. 39-41.]' plus a short comparative list (páru, kampón, nunó, yó) copied with accents from Krause.

sources.citation: Baldus, Herbert. 1954. Bibliografia Crítica da Etnologia Brasileira, vol. I, item 0777 (summary of Krause 1936), via Etnolinguistica
sources.note: Nothing; notes only that Meyer's vocabulary (pp. 39-41) shows close kinship of Yarumá with Apiaká do Tocantins.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid page yaru1255 and reference record 142191 (Krause 1936, doctype wordlist, cites p. 41); other refs listed there: Lévi-Strauss 1948 (HSAI), Galvão & Simões 1965, Villas Boas & Villas Boas 1972 (ethnographic)

Krause, Fritz. 1936. Die Yarumá- und Arawine-Indianer Zentralbrasiliens. Baessler-Archiv 19(1-2): 32-44. Berlin. (Etnolinguistica/Biblioteca Digital Curt Nimuendajú PDF of the digi-hub.de scan, with scanned text layer)
sources.note: Nothing. Sec. 3 'Sprachaufnahmen' (p. 38) only describes how Meyer obtained the lists; the Yarumá wordlists A-C (pp. 39-41) carry acute accent marks, predominantly on the final syllable (üvóri, uén, yeinát, yerinapún, yempitpún, irarepún, yembén, yemearé, yamóin, evún, üpún, kavón, tzizí, nunó, tsirín; exception yémuru), but no rule or remark on Betonung/Akzent anywhere in the article (grep + page reads of pp. 32, 34, 38-41, 44; p. 39 checked against the page image).

sources.citation: Steinen, Karl von den. 1894. Unter den Naturvölkern Zentral-Brasiliens. Berlin: Reimer. (archive.org scanned held)
sources.note: Nothing; only hearsay ethnographic mentions of the 'Yarumá oder Arumá' (pp. 118, 155, 392), no language data.

sources.citation: Meira, Sérgio & Bruna Franchetto. 2005. The Southern Cariban languages and the Cariban family. International Journal of American Linguistics 71(2): 127-192.

sources.note: Only modern linguistic treatment of Yarumá: re-transcribes and etymologises Krause's 1936 list against Bakairi, Ikpeng, Arara, Kuikuro; if anyone has commented on what Meyer's accent marks mean (final stress like Arara/Ikpeng vs. informant artefact), it is here. Would supersede the bare wordlist reading.

sources.citation: Meyer, Herrmann. Manuscript field notebooks R III 6 (pp. 80-81, 'Uraufnahme' of the Yarumá vocabulary), R III 20, R VI 7; Nachlass Herrmann Meyer, Archiv des Museums für Völkerkunde zu Leipzig (GRASSI), as cited by Krause 1936 p. 38.
